q: In the preparation of some pure crystals of Cu (NO₃)₂ starting with CuO, a student gave the following statements as steps he employed. Which of these shows a flaw in his report?
opts: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H₂SO₄
When the concentrate was cooled, crystals formed were removed by filtration.
The crystals were washed with very cold water
The crystals were then allowed to dry.
exp: To prepare Cu(NO₃)₂ the acid must be dilute HNO₃. Using H₂SO₄ gives CuSO₄ crystals instead — that is the flaw.

q: Which of the following methods may be used to prepare trioxonirate (V) acid (nitric acid) in the laboratory?
opts: Heating ammonia gas with tetraoxosulphate (IV) acid
Heating ammonium trioxosulphate (V) with tetraoxonitrate (V) acid
Heating sodium trioxonirate (v) with tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
Heating potassium trioxonirate (V) with calcium hydroxide.
Heating a mixture of ammonia gas and oxygen\
exp: Nitric acid is prepared in the lab by heating sodium trioxonitrate(V) (NaNO₃) with concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid: NaNO₃ + H₂SO₄ → NaHSO₄ + HNO₃.

q: Nitrogen can best be obtained from a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen by passing the mixture over
exp: Heated phosphorus burns in the oxygen to form solid P₂O₅, which is easily removed, leaving nitrogen. It removes oxygen most completely.

q: Which of the following substances is a mixture?
exp: Sea-water contains dissolved salts and other substances in no fixed proportion — a mixture. The others are pure substances.

q: Some products of destructive distillation of coal are
exp: Destructive distillation of coal yields coke, coal gas, coal tar and ammoniacal liquor.

q: Mortar is NOT used for under-water construction because.
opts: It hardens by loss of water
Its hardening does not depent upon evaporation
It will be washed away by the flow of water.
exp: Mortar sets by losing water and absorbing CO₂ from air; under water it cannot dry or absorb CO₂, so it never hardens.

q: To make coloured glasses, small quantities of oxides of metals which form coloured silicates are often added to the reaction mixture consisting of Na₂CO₃ and SO₂. Such a metal is
exp: Copper(II) oxide gives glass a blue-green colour because copper forms coloured silicates. K, Ba and Zn silicates are colourless.

q: Which of the following can be obtained by fraction of distillation?
opts: Iodine from a solution of iodine in carbon tetrachloride
Sulphur from a solution of sulphur in carbon disulphide.
exp: Liquid air is separated into nitrogen and oxygen by fractional distillation using their different boiling points (N₂ −196°C, O₂ −183°C).

q: Which of the following substances is not a homogeneous mixture?
exp: Flood water carries suspended mud and debris — visibly different phases, so it is heterogeneous. The others are uniform solutions.

q: For iodine crystals to sublime on heating, the molecules must acquire energy that is
opts: less than the forces of attraction in the solid
equal to the forces of attraction in the solid
greater than the forces of attraction in both solid and the liquid phases
exp: Sublimation goes directly from solid to gas, so molecules must gain enough energy to overcome attractive forces of both the solid and liquid phases.

q: An experiment produces a gaseous mixture of carbon (IV) oxide and carbon(II) Oxide. In order to obtain pure carbon (II) oxide, the gas mixture should be
exp: NaOH solution absorbs the acidic CO₂ (forming Na₂CO₃), letting pure CO pass through unaffected.

q: A pure solid usually melts
opts: over a wide range of temperature
over a narrow range of temperature
at a lower temperature than the impure one
at the same temperature as the impure one.
exp: A pure solid has a sharp melting point (narrow range); impurities lower and broaden the melting range.

q: Alloys are often used in preference to pure metals bacause
opts: metallic properties are improved in alloys
alloys are a mixture of metals. OH
exp: Alloying improves properties — strength, hardness, corrosion resistance — compared with the pure metals.

q: What is observed when aqueous solution of each of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, potassium trioxides (V) and potassium iodine are mixed together?
exp: In acid solution, iodate(V) oxidises iodide to iodine: IO₃⁻ + 5I⁻ + 6H⁺ → 3I₂ + 3H₂O. The liberated iodine turns the mixture reddish-brown.

q: Sieving is a technique used to separate mixtures containing solid particles of
exp: Sieving separates solid particles of different sizes — small particles pass through the mesh while larger ones are retained.

q: Synthesic gas is a mixture of
exp: Synthesis gas (water gas) is a mixture of carbon(II) oxide and hydrogen, made by passing steam over hot coke.

q: Which of the following mixtures of gases is likely to burn in flame?
exp: Hydrogen is flammable, so a neon–hydrogen mixture can burn. Helium, neon and nitrogen are all non-combustible.

q: Which if the following solution will give a white precipitate with barium chloride solution and a green flame test?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: A sulphate gives a white BaSO₄ precipitate with BaCl₂, and copper gives a green flame — so the salt is CuSO₄.

q: A jet plane carrying 3,000 kg of ethane burns off all the gas forming water and carbondioxide. If all the carbondioxide is expelled and the water formed is condensed and kept on board the plane, then the gain in weight is
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: C₂H₆ (M=30) gives 3H₂O (54 g per 30 g ethane). Water kept = 3000 × 54/30 = 5400 kg; ethane lost = 3000 kg; net gain = 2400 kg.

q: 30cm³ of 0.1 M AI(NO₃)₃ solution is reacted with 100cm³ of 0.15M of NaOH solution. Which is in excess and by how much?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Al(NO₃)₃: 3 mmol needs 9 mmol OH⁻. NaOH supplied = 15 mmol, excess = 6 mmol = 6/0.15 = 40 cm³ of the NaOH solution.

q: Manganese (IV) oxide reacts with concentrated hydrochloric acid according to the equation MnO₂ + xHCI MnCI₂ + CI +yH₂O. x and y are
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Balanced: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O, so x = 4 and y = 2.

q: Naphthalene when heated melts at 354K (81oC) . At this temperature the molecules of naphthalene .
opts: become mobile as the inter molecular forces are broken.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: On melting, the crystal lattice breaks down — intermolecular forces are overcome and the molecules become mobile.

q: Which of the following structure formulae is NOT numeric with others?
opts: H H H H | | | | H–C- C - C – OH | | | | H H H H
H H H H | | | | H–C- O- C - C – C- H | | | | H H H H
H H H H | | | | H–C- C - C – C- H | | | | H OH H H
H O H | | H–C- C - C – C- H | | | | H H H H
H H O H | | H–C - C - C – C- H | | | | H H H H
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Option A is propan-1-ol (C₃H₈O, three carbons); the others are four-carbon compounds, so A is not isomeric with them.

q: 0.499 of CuSO₄.xH₂O when heated to constant weight gave a residue of 0.346 g. The value of x is
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Residue CuSO₄ = 0.346/159.5 = 0.00217 mol; water lost = 0.153/18 = 0.0085 mol; ratio ≈ 4, so x = 4.

q: When pollen grains are suspended in water and viewed through a microscope, they appear to be in a state of constant but erratic motion. This is due to
opts: a chemical reaction between the pollen grains and water
the bombardment of the pollen grains by molecules of water.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: This is Brownian motion — the pollen grains are being bombarded randomly by fast-moving water molecules.

q: Addition of dilute hydrochloric acid to an aqueous solution of a crystalline salt yielded a yellow precipitate and a gas which turned dichromate paper green. The crystalline salt was probably
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Thiosulphate + HCl gives a yellow precipitate of sulphur and SO₂ gas (turns dichromate paper green): S₂O₃²⁻ + 2H⁺ → S + SO₂ + H₂O.

q: 10cm³ of hydrogen fluoride gas reacts with 5cm³ of dinitrogen difllouride gas (N₂F₂) to form 10cm³ of a single gas. Which of the following is the most likely equation to the reaction?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Volume ratio 10:5:10 = 2:1:2, matching 2HF + N₂F₂ → 2NHF₂ (Gay-Lussac's law).

q: Which of the following solution will conduct the least amount of electricity?
opts: 0.01 m aqueous solution of hexaonic acid
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Sugar is a non-electrolyte — its solution contains no ions, so it conducts least.

q: How many electrons are transferred in reducing one atom of Mn in the reaction MnO₂ + 4HCl MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Mn goes from +4 in MnO₂ to +2 in MnCl₂ — a gain of 2 electrons.

q: What are the values of x, y and z respectively in the equation xCu +yHNO₃ xCu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + zNO?s
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Balanced: 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + 2NO, so x, y, z = 3, 8, 2.

q: Which of the following compounds would give lilac fame coloration and a white precipitate with acidified barium chloride solution?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Lilac flame = potassium; white precipitate with acidified BaCl₂ = sulphate. Hence K₂SO₄.

q: Complete oxidation of propan – 1 – of gives
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: A primary alcohol oxidises via the aldehyde to the carboxylic acid: propan-1-ol → propanal → propanoic acid.

q: 2.25 g of sample of an oxide of a copper. 2.50 g of another oxide of Copper on reduction also gave2.0 g of copper. These results are in accordance with the law of
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: The same mass of copper combines with different masses of oxygen in the two oxides — the law of multiple proportions.

q: An increase in temperature causes an increase in the pressure in the
opts: number of collisions between the molecules
free mean path between each molecules and other.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Raising temperature increases the average velocity (kinetic energy) of molecules, so they strike the walls harder and more often.

q: Smoke consists of
opts: solid or liquid particles dispersed in gas
gas or liquid particles dispersed in liquid
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Smoke is an aerosol — solid (or liquid) particles dispersed in a gas.

q: Cr₂O₇ above chromium change from.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: In Cr₂O₇²⁻ chromium is +6; on reduction to Cr³⁺ it changes from +6 to +3.

q: The brown fumes given off when trioxonirate (V) acid consist of
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: HNO₃ decomposes: 4HNO₃ → 4NO₂ + O₂ + 2H₂O, so the brown fumes contain NO₂, O₂ and water vapour.

q: Sodium hydroxide should be stored in properly closed containers because it
opts: readily absorbs water vapour from the air
is easily oxidized by atmospheric oxygen
turns golden yellow when exposed to light.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: NaOH is deliquescent — it absorbs water vapour (and CO₂) from air, so it must be kept tightly closed.

q: A given quantity of gas occupies a volume of 228 cm³ at a pressure of 750 mm Hg. What will be its volume at atmospheric pressure?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Boyle's law: V₂ = 228 × 750/760 = 225 cm³.

q: Which of the following gases will rekindle a brightly glowing splint?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Dinitrogen oxide (N₂O) supports combustion and rekindles a glowing splint, like oxygen.

q: Which of the following salts can be melted without decomposition?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Na₂CO₃ is stable to heat and melts without decomposing; CaCO₃, MgCO₃ and ZnCO₃ all decompose to their oxides.

q: How many grams of bromine will be required to completely react with 10 g of propyne?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Propyne C₃H₄ (M=40): 10 g = 0.25 mol; the triple bond adds 2Br₂, so 0.5 mol Br₂ = 0.5 × 160 = 80 g.

q: A given mass of gas occupies 2 dm³ at 300 K. At what temperature will its volume be doubled keeping the pressure constant?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Charles' law: doubling volume at constant pressure needs double the absolute temperature: 2 × 300 = 600 K.

q: Water for town supply is chlorinate to make it free from
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Chlorination kills bacteria and other germs in the water supply.

q: How many grams of H₂SO₄ are necessary for the preparation of 0.175 dm³ of 6.00 M H₂SO₄?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws

q: Addition of an aqueous solution of barium chloride to the aqueous solution of a salt gives a white precipate.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Of the options, only carbonate forms a white insoluble precipitate (BaCO₃) with barium chloride.

q: At 25oC and 1 atm, a gas occupies a volume of 1.50 dm³. What volume will it occupy at 100oC at 1 atm?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Charles' law: V₂ = 1.50 × 373/298 = 1.88 dm³.

q: Which group of elements forms hydrides that are pyramidal in structure?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Group V hydrides (e.g. NH₃, PH₃) have one lone pair and three bonds — pyramidal shape.

q: To what temperature must a gas 273 K be heated in order to double both its volume and pressure?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: P₁V₁/T1 = P₂V₂/T2: doubling both P and V requires T2 = 4 × 273 = 1092 K.

q: A liquid begins to boil when
opts: its vapour pressure is equal to vapour pressure of its solid at the given temperature
molecules start escaping from its surface
its vapour pressure equals the atmosheric pressure
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: A liquid boils when its saturated vapour pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure.

q: Helium is often used in observation balloons because it is
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Helium is very light and, unlike hydrogen, completely non-combustible — safe for balloons.

q: Which of the following processes lead to increase in entrophy?
opts: mixing a sample of NaCl and sand
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Boiling converts liquid to vapour — a large increase in disorder (entropy). The other processes decrease or barely change it.

q: Which of the following compound will impart a brick- red colour to a non-luminous Busen flame?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Calcium compounds give the characteristic brick-red flame colour.

q: A satyrated solution of AgCI was found to have a concentration of 1.30 x 100-5 mol dm⁻³. The solution product of AgCI. therefore is.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws

q: What is the oxidation unmber of Z in K³ ZCI₆ ?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws

q: The soil around a battery manufacturing factory is likely to contain a high concentration of
opts: AI₃+ salts. 90.0 g of MgCI₂ was placed in 50.0cm³ of water to give a
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Battery factories work with lead(II) compounds (lead-acid batteries), contaminating soil with Pb²⁺ salts.

q: The oxide that remains unchanged when heated in hydrogen is
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Hydrogen only reduces oxides of metals below it in the activity series (Cu, Pb, Fe). Zinc is above hydrogen, so ZnO is unchanged.

q: Which of the following is true concerning the properties of benezene and hexane?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution and hexane undergoes free-radical substitution — both substitute; neither readily adds or decolourises bromine water.

q: In which of the following are water molecules in the most disorderly arrangement?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Steam is a gas — its molecules are in the most random, disorderly arrangement.

q: Hydrogen is used in oxy-hydrogen flames for melting metals because it
opts: evolves a lot of heat when burnt
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Hydrogen burning in oxygen is highly exothermic, giving a flame hot enough to melt metals.

q: What properties of duralumin make it more useful than its constituent metals?
opts: it is heavy with a high melting point
it is malleable and has high density
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Duralumin (Al alloy) combines strength with lightness — better than its constituent metals alone.

q: How many grammes of bromine will saturate 5.2 g of but-l-ene-3-yne?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: But-1-ene-3-yne C₄H₄ (M=52): 5.2 g = 0.1 mol; saturation needs 3Br₂ (one for C=C, two for C≡C) = 0.3 × 160 = 48 g.

q: Polyvinyl chloride is used to produced
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: PVC is widely used for pipes, cable insulation and similar products.

q: Which of the compounds is composed of Al, Si, O and H?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Clay is hydrated aluminium silicate — made of Al, Si, O and H.

q: Hydration of ions in solution is associated with
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Hydration of ions is exothermic — energy is liberated when water molecules surround the ions.

q: In which order are the following salts sensitive to light?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Photosensitivity order used in photography: AgBr > AgCl > AgI — AgBr is the standard light-sensitive salt in film.

q: Powdered marble reacts with hydrochloric acid solution than the granular form because the powdered form has
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Powdering increases surface area, exposing more particles to the acid so reaction is faster.

q: 25cm³ of a gas X contains Z molecules at 15oC and 75 mm Hg. How many molecules will 25cm³ of another gas Y contain at the same temperature and pressure?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Avogadro's law: equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules — Z.

q: What is the decrease in volume of air when pyrogallol is shaken with 30.00cm³ of air?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Pyrogallol absorbs oxygen (≈21% of air): 30.00 × 0.21 = 6.30 cm³ decrease.

q: As the concentration of an electrolyte reduces, the conductivity
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Fewer ions per unit volume means lower conductivity as the electrolyte is diluted.

q: Ethanoic acid is
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Ethanoic acid CH₃COOH has only one ionisable hydrogen — monobasic.

q: In which of the following reactions does reduction take place?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Reduction is electron gain: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. The others lose electrons (oxidation).

q: A rock sample was added to cold dilute HNO₃. The gas evolved was passed into a solution of acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ and the solution turned green. The rock sample contains.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: The gas that turns acidified dichromate green is SO₂, evolved from a trioxosulphate(IV) (sulphite, SO₃²⁻) in the rock.

q: Ordinary glass is manufactured from silica, CaCO₃ and
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Ordinary (soda-lime) glass is made from silica, limestone (CaCO₃) and sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) Na₂CO₃.

q: Which of these pairs are synthetic and natural macromolecules respectively?
opts: Nylon and polyethylene, creatine and haemoglobin
Nylon and creative, polyethylene and haemoglobin
Polyethylene and creatine, nylon and haemoglobin
Haemoglobin and nylon, creatine and polyethylene
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Nylon and polyethylene are synthetic polymers; creatine and haemoglobin are natural macromolecules.

q: Hydrogen is readily released when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Only sodium is above hydrogen in the activity series among the options — Ag, Au and Cu do not displace hydrogen from HCl.

q: A fixed mass of gas has a volume of 92 cm³ at 3oC. What will be its volume at 18oC if the pressure remains constant?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Charles' law: V₂ = 92 × 291/276 = 97.0 cm³.

q: Steam changes the colour of anhydrous cobalt (II) chloride from
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Anhydrous CoCl₂ (blue) turns pink on contact with water/steam — the classic test for water.

q: A gas exerts pressure on its container because
opts: some of its molecules are moving faster than others
of the collision of the molecules with each other
of the mass of the molecules of gas
the molecules of a gas collide with walls of the container.
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Gas pressure arises from molecules colliding with the container walls.

q: Which of the following shows little or not net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased?
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI has equal moles of gas on both sides, so volume (pressure) change does not shift it.

q: A chemical reaction is always associated with
opts: a change in the nature of the reactants
a change in the volume of the reactants
an increase in the composition of one of the substances,
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: A chemical reaction always produces new substances — the defining feature.

q: It is difficult to achieve an orderly arrangement of the molecules of a gas because they.
opts: can collide with one another in the container
have little force of attraction between them
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Gas molecules have negligible attractive forces between them, so they cannot hold an orderly arrangement.

q: Aluminum hydroxide is used in the dyeing industry as a
topic: Particulate Nature of Matter & Chemical Laws
exp: Aluminium hydroxide acts as a mordant — it fixes dyes onto fabric.

q: If an element has the lectronic configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p2, it is
exp: The outermost electrons are filling a p subshell (3p²), so the element (silicon) is a p-block element.

q: The mass of an atom is determined by
opts: the number of neutrons and protons
the number of neutrons and electrons
exp: Nearly all of an atom's mass is in the nucleus — the protons and neutrons (nucleons).

q: The atomic number of an element whose caution, X2+, has the ground state electronic configuration is Is22s22P₆₃s22p6 is
exp: X²⁺ has 18 electrons, so the neutral atom has 20 — atomic number 20 (calcium).

q: An element with atomic number twelve is likely to be
exp: Z = 12 is magnesium (2,8,2): it loses its 2 outer electrons, forming ionic (electrovalent) compounds with valency 2.

q: An isotope has an atomic number of 17 and a mass number of 36. Which of the following gives the correct number of neutrons and protons in an atom of the isotope? Neutrons Protons
exp: Protons = atomic number = 17; neutrons = 36 − 17 = 19.

q: The atomic numbers of two elements X and Y are 12 and 9 respectively. The bond in the compound formed between the atoms of these two elements is.
exp: X (Z=12) is a metal (Mg) and Y (Z=9) a reactive non-metal (F): electron transfer gives an ionic bond.

q: A metallic ion X2+ with an inert gas structure contain 18 electrons. How many protons are there in this ion?
exp: X²⁺ with 18 electrons means the neutral atom had 20 electrons, so it has 20 protons.

q: The atomic radius Li, Na and K are 1:33 A m 1.54A and 1.96A respectively. Which of the following explain this gradation in atomic radius?
opts: Electropositivity decreases from Li to Na to K
Electronegativity decreases from Li to Na to K.
The number of electron shells increase from Li to Ma to K
The elements are in the same period.
exp: Down the group each element adds an extra electron shell, so the atomic radius increases from Li to Na to K.

q: Elements X and Y have electronic configurations 1s22s22p4 and 1s22s22p63s23p1 respectively. When they combine, the formula of the compound formed is
exp: X (2p⁴) is oxygen, valency 2; Y (3p¹) is aluminium, valency 3 — they form Y2X3 (Al₂O₃).

q: The atomic number of cesium is 55 and its atomic mass is 133. The nucleus of cesium atom therefore contains
exp: Protons = 55 (atomic number); neutrons = 133 − 55 = 78.

q: Four elements P,Q,R and S have atomic numbers of 4, 10, 12, and 14 respectively. Which of these elements is a noble gas?
exp: Q has atomic number 10 — neon, a noble gas with a complete octet.

q: How many valence electrons are contained in the element represented by 31 15P?
exp: ³¹₁₅P has configuration 2,8,5 — five valence electrons.

q: Proton 13 16 17 19 Electron 13 16 17 19 Neutron 14 16 35 20 Which of the four atoms P,Q,R and S in the above data can be described by the following properties: relative atomic mass is greater than 30 but less than 40 ; it has an odd atomic number and forms a unipositive ion in solution?
exp: S: 19 protons + 20 neutrons = mass 39 (between 30 and 40), odd atomic number 19, and potassium forms K⁺ — all conditions met.

q: Chlorine, consisting of two isotope of mass numbers 35 and 37, has an atomic of 35.5. The relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37 is.
The electronic configuration of an element is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3. How many unpaired electron are there in the element.
exp: 3p³ places one electron in each of the three p orbitals (Hund's rule) — 3 unpaired electrons.

q: The nucleus of the isotope tritium, contains
opts: two neutron, one proton, and one electron.
exp: Tritium (³H) has one proton and two neutrons in its nucleus (the atom also carries one electron).

q: 14 N + X 17 8 O + 1 1 H . In the above reaction , X is a
exp: Balancing mass (14 + 4 = 17 + 1) and charge (7 + 2 = 8 + 1) shows X is ⁴₂He — a helium nucleus (alpha particle).

q: Four elements P,Q,R and S have 1,2,3 and 7 electrons in their outermost shells respectively. The element which is unlikely to be a metal is
exp: S has 7 outer electrons — a halogen-type non-metal. Elements with 1–3 outer electrons are typically metals.

q: The number of electrons in the valence shell of an element of atomic number 14 is
exp: Z = 14 (silicon): configuration 2,8,4 — four valence electrons.

q: Which of the following atoms represents deuterium? ‘ No of No of No of protons neutrons electrons
exp: Deuterium (²H) has 1 proton, 1 neutron and 1 electron.

q: A particle that contains 8 protons, 9 neutrons and 7 electrons could be written as
exp: 8 protons + 9 neutrons = mass 17; 7 electrons vs 8 protons = +1 charge: the particle is ¹⁷₈O⁺.

q: In the oil drop experiment, Milikan determined the
opts: charge to mass ratio of the electron
exp: Millikan's oil drop experiment measured the charge on the electron.

q: In the periodic table, what is the property that decrease along the period and increases down the group
exp: Atomic radius decreases across a period (greater nuclear pull) and increases down a group (more shells).

q: Two elements, P and Q with atomic numbers 11 and 8 respectively, combine chemically values of x and y are
exp: P (Z=11) is Na, valency 1; Q (Z=8) is O, valency 2 → Na₂O, so x = 2 and y = 1.

q: Oxygen is a mixture of two isotopes 16 8 O and 18 8 O with relative abundance of 90% and 10% respectively. The relative atomic mass of oxygen
Which of the following electron configurations indicates an atom with the highest ionization energy?
exp: 2,8,7 is chlorine — a small halogen close to a full octet; it holds its electrons most tightly of the options.

q: The lines observe in the simple hydrogen spectrum are due to emission of
exp: Spectral lines come from electrons falling between energy levels, emitting fixed quanta of energy.

q: ls22s22p63s23p63d74s2. An element with the electron configuration above is a
exp: A partially filled 3d subshell (3d⁷) makes it a transition element.

q: Which of the following the following statements is correct about the periodic table?
opts: Element in the same period have the same number of valence electrons
The valence electrons of the elements in the same period increase progressively across the period
Elements in the same group have the number of electron shells
The non-metallic properties of the elements tent to decrease across each period
exp: Across a period the number of valence electrons increases progressively from 1 to 8.

q: The knowledge of half-life can be used to
exp: Half-life is characteristic of each radioisotope, so it can be used to detect/identify an element (e.g. carbon dating).

q: Four elements W,X,Y and Z have atomic numbers 2,6,16 and 20 respectively. Which of these elements is a meal?

the crystal lattice of metals is easily broken.

exp: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules require extra energy to break, raising the boiling point far above similar-sized molecules.

shape of the container they occupy
degree of movement of their particles

exp: Metallic bonding holds atoms of one element together — no new substance is formed, unlike compound-forming bonds.

exp: CO₂ is linear, H₂O is bent (two lone pairs), CH₄ is tetrahedral.

exp: Van der Waals forces are the weakest intermolecular attractions.

its ions dissolve readily in water
it has a tendency to lose electrons
it has a tendency to gain electrons
exp: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract (gain) electrons in a bond.

exp: Across a period the increasing nuclear charge pulls the shells in — atomic radius decreases.

exp: Electron affinity is the energy change when a gaseous atom gains an electron.

exp: Across period 3 electronegativity rises: Na < Mg < Al < P < Cl.

exp: A greater electronegativity difference means the shared electrons sit more unevenly — the bond becomes more polar.

exp: Down a group atoms get larger and attract bonding electrons less — electronegativity decreases.

exp: Activated wood charcoal adsorbs poisonous gases (gas masks) and is used to purify noble gases.

q: In the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia, the catalyst commonly used is finely divided.
exp: Finely divided iron catalyses N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃.

q: Manganese(IV) oxide is known to hasten the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. Its main actions is to.
opts: increase the surface area of the reactants
increase the concentration of the reactants
lower the activation energy for the reaction
lower the heat of reaction, H, for the reaction,
exp: A catalyst provides an alternative path with a lower activation energy.

q: If the rate law obtained for a given reaction is rate=k(X)n(Y)m, what is the overall order of the reaction?
exp: Overall order is the sum of the individual orders: n + m.

q: In order to remove one electron from 3s-orbital of gaseous sodium atom, about 496 kJ mol⁻¹ of energy is required. This energy is referred to as
exp: Energy to remove an electron from a gaseous atom is the ionization energy.

q: Which of the following best explains the increase in the rate of a chemical reaction as the temperature rises?
opts: A lower proportion of the molecules has the necessary minimum energy to react
The bonds in the reacting molecules are more readily broken
The collision frequency of the molecules increases
The molecular collisions become more violent.
exp: At higher temperature collisions are more energetic, so far more of them exceed the activation energy.

q: P(g) + Q(g) 3R(s)+S(g) which of the following will increase the yield of R?
exp: Removing product S pulls the equilibrium forward, making more R (Le Chatelier).

q: The Arrhenius equation expresses the relationship between the speed of a reaction and its
exp: The Arrhenius equation k = Ae^(−Ea/RT) links rate to activation energy.

q: Which of the following will change when a catalyst is added to a chemical reaction?
opts: The potential energy of the reactants
The potential energy of the products.
exp: A catalyst changes only the activation energy — not the enthalpies of reactants, products, or the reaction.

q: The equilibrium reaction between copper (I) chloride and chloride at 25oC and 1 atmosphere is represented by the equation: 2CuCI₂ + CI₂ 2CuCI₂ H = -166kJ . Which of the following statement is TRUE for the reaction, pressure remaining constant. is formed at 40oC
opts: Less CuCI₂ is formed at 10oC D there is no change CuCI₂ formed at 40oC and 10oC
exp: The forward reaction is exothermic, so lower temperature (10°C) favours more CuCl₂.

q: X + Y Z is an equilibrium reaction. The addition of a catalyst
opts: increases the amount of W produced in a given time
increase the rate of change in concentrations of X, Y and Z
increases the rate of disappearance of X and Y
increases the rate of the forward reaction
decreases the amounts of X and Y left after the attainment of equilibrium.
exp: A catalyst speeds both directions equally — concentrations change faster but the equilibrium position is unchanged.

q: In the reaction H₂O(g)’! H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) H=-2436000kJ2, which of the following has no effect on the equilibrium position?
exp: Adding an inert gas at constant volume changes no partial pressures — no effect on the equilibrium.

q: What is the consequence of increasing pressure on the equilibrium reaction ZnO(s) + H₂(g Zn(s) + H₂O(i)
opts: The equilibrium is driven to the left
The equilibrium is driven to the right
exp: Gas moles fall from 1 (H₂) to 0 (H₂O is liquid), so higher pressure drives the equilibrium to the right.

q: The reaction between sulphur (IV) oxide and oxygen is represented by the equilibrium reaction 2SO₂(g H + O₂(g) 2SO₃(g), H = - 196 kJ. What factor would influence increased production SO₃(g)?
opts: Increase in the temperature of the reaction
Decrease in the temperature of SO₂(g)
Decrease in the concentration of SO₂(g)
exp: The reaction is exothermic, so lowering the temperature favours SO₃ formation.

q: Which property of reversible reaction is affected by a catalyst?
exp: A catalyst lowers the activation energy only; enthalpy, ΔG and the equilibrium position are unchanged.

q: A basic postulate of the kinetic theory of gases is that the molecules of a gas move in straight lines between collisions. This implies that.
opts: forces of repulsion and attraction are in equilibrium
collisions are inelastic. P Q R S
exp: Straight-line motion between collisions means no net intermolecular force acts — attraction and repulsion balance out (are negligible).

q: In the reaction , 2Hl(g) H₂(g) + I₂(g), H = 10 kJ; the concentration of iodine in the equilibrium mixture can be increased by
exp: The forward reaction is endothermic (+10 kJ), so raising the temperature makes more iodine.

q: Which of the following equilibria is unaffected by a pressure change?
exp: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI has 2 gas moles on each side — pressure has no effect.

q: In what way is equilibrium constant for the forward reaction related to that that of the reverse reaction?
opts: The addition of the two is expected to be one
The product of the two is expected to be one
The two equilibrium constants are identical
The product of the two is always greater than one.
exp: K(forward) × K(reverse) = 1 — they are reciprocals.

q: Which of the following equilibra shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the volume of the system is decreased?
exp: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI has equal gas moles both sides, so volume change causes no net shift.

q: For a general equation of the nature xP + yQ mR + nS, the expression for the equilibrium constant is
exp: K = [R]^m[S]^n / [P]^x[Q]^y — products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient.

q: 10 g of a solid is in equilibrium with its own vapour. When 1 g of a small amount of solid is added, the vapour pressure
exp: Vapour pressure depends only on temperature, not on how much solid is present.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of Le Chatelier’s principle for an exothermic reaction?
opts: Increase in temperature will cause an increase in equilibrium constant
Increase in temperature will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant
Addition of catalyst will cause an increase in the equilibrium constant.
Addition of catalyst will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant.
exp: For an exothermic reaction, raising the temperature shifts equilibrium backward — K decreases.

q: If an equilibrium reaction has “H < O, the reaction will proceed favourably in the forward reaction at
exp: ΔH < 0 (exothermic): low temperatures favour the forward reaction.

q: 2CI₂(g) + 2H₂O(g) 4HCI(g) +O₂(g) Ho = +115kJ mol⁻¹ In the above equilibrium reaction a decrease in temperature will.
opts: have no effect on the equilibrium state
double the rate of the reverse reaction
exp: The forward reaction is endothermic (+115 kJ); cooling favours the exothermic reverse reaction.

q: For a reaction in equilibrium, the species involved in the equilibrium constant expression are
exp: Only gases and dissolved species appear in K expressions; pure solids and liquids are omitted.

q: Which of the following equations shows that a reaction is in equilibrium?
exp: At equilibrium the free energy change is zero: ΔG = 0.

q: A change in the temperature of a saturated solution disturbs the equilibrium between the
opts: Dissolved solute and the undissolved solute
exp: In a saturated solution the equilibrium is between dissolved and undissolved solute.

q: If an equilibrium reaction has H > 0, the reaction will proceed favourable in the forward direction.
exp: ΔH > 0 (endothermic): high temperature drives the reaction forward.

q: When at equilibrium, which of the reactions below will shift to the right if the pressure is increased and the temperature is kept constant .
exp: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O goes from 3 gas moles to 2 — increased pressure shifts it right.

q: In which of the following processes is iron being oxidized? 1. Fe + H₂SO₄ H₂ + FeSO₄ 2. FeSO₄+ H₂S FeS + H₂SO₄ 3 FeCl + CI₂ 2FeCL3 4 FeCl₃ + SnCI₂ 2FeCL2 + SnCI₄
exp: Iron is oxidised in 1 (0 → +2) and in 3 (FeCl₂ → FeCl₃, +2 → +3); in 2 and 4 its oxidation number falls or is on the product side.

q: Which of the following pair of gases will NOT react further with oxygen at a temperature between 30oC and 400oC?
exp: NO₂ and SO₃ are already the higher oxides — they do not combine further with oxygen.

q: Which among the element 1. Carbon 2. Oxygen 3. Copper 4. Bromine 5. Zinc will NOT react with either water of stream?
exp: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam; carbon and zinc react with steam, bromine reacts slightly with water.

q: The ration of the number of molecules in 2g of hydrogen to that in 16 g of oxygen is
exp: 2 g H₂ = 1 mol; 16 g O₂ = 0.5 mol → 2:1 ratio of molecules.

q: Lime –water, which is used in the laboratory for the detection of carbon (IV) oxide, is an aqueous solution of:
exp: Lime water is a dilute aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2.

q: An example of a neutral oxide is
exp: CO is a neutral oxide; NO₂, CO₂ and SO₂ are acidic and Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.

q: Which of the following conducts electricity?
exp: Graphite has delocalised electrons between its layers — the only non-metal listed that conducts.

q: In what respect will two dry samples of nitrogen gas differ from each other if samples 1 is prepared by completely removing CO₂ and O₂ from air and sample 2 is prepared by passing purified nitrogen (i) oxide over heated copper? Sample 1 is
opts: in all respects the same as sample 2
colourless but sample 2 has a light brown.
exp: Nitrogen from air still contains the denser noble gases (mainly argon), so sample 1 is slightly denser.

q: Which of the following is used in the manufacture of bleaching powder?
exp: Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over slaked lime.

q: Tetraoxosulphate (VI) ions are finally tested using
exp: SO₄²⁻ gives a white precipitate of BaSO₄ with acidified barium chloride, insoluble in the acid.

q: Which of the following substances is the most abundant in the universe?
exp: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe.

q: An aqueous solution of an inorganic salt gave white precipate (i) soluble in excess aqueous NaOH (ii) insoluble in excess aqueous NH₃ (III) with dilute HCI. The caution present in the inorganic salt is
exp: A white precipitate with dilute HCl (PbCl₂) plus hydroxide behaviour soluble in NaOH but not NH₃ identifies Pb²⁺.

q: How much of magnesium is required to react with 250cm³ of 0.5 M HCl?
exp: HCl = 0.125 mol; Mg + 2HCl needs 0.0625 mol Mg = 1.5 g.

q: The approximate volume of air containing 10cm of oxygen is
exp: Air is about 21% oxygen, so 10 cm³ O₂ comes from roughly 50 cm³ of air.

q: When steam is passed through red hot carbon, which of the following are produced?
opts: Hydrogen and oxygen and carbon(IV) oxide
exp: C + H₂O → CO + H₂ (water gas) when steam passes over red-hot carbon.

q: Which of the following will react further with oxygen to form a higher oxide?
exp: SO₂ → SO₃ and NO → NO₂ — both form higher oxides with more oxygen.

q: Which of the following sulphides is insoluble in dilute HCl?
exp: CuS is insoluble in dilute HCl; the sulphides of Na, Zn and Fe dissolve, evolving H₂S.

q: When chlorine is passes into water and subsequently exposed to sunlight, the gas evolved is
exp: Sunlight decomposes chlorine water: 2HOCl → 2HCl + O₂ — the gas is oxygen.

q: Which of the following metals does NOT form a stable trioxocarbonate(IV)
exp: Aluminium carbonate is not stable — Al³⁺ hydrolyses too strongly for a stable trioxocarbonate.

q: Ammonia gas is normally dried with
exp: Ammonia is dried with quicklime (CaO); H₂SO₄ and CaCl₂ react with it.

q: A white solid suspected to be lead trioxonirate (V), zinc trioxocarbonate(IV) of calcium trioxocarbonate (IV) was heated strongly. Its residue, which was yellow when hot and white when cold, is
exp: Zinc oxide is yellow when hot and white when cold — the classic identifying property.

q: The number of molecules of carbon (IV) oxide produced when 10.0 g CaCO₃ is treated with 0.2 dm³ of 1 M HCl in the equation CaCO₃ + 2HCI CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂ is
exp: HCl (0.2 mol) limits the reaction: 0.1 mol CO₂ = 0.1 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²² molecules.

q: A stream of air was successively passed through three tubes X, Y, and Z containing a concentrated aqueous solution of KOH, red hot copper powder and fused calcium chloride respectively. What was the composition of gas emanating from tube Z?
opts: N₂, CO₂ and the inert gases
Water vapour, N₂ and the inert gases.
exp: KOH removes CO₂, hot copper removes O₂, CaCl₂ removes moisture — leaving nitrogen and the inert gases.

q: If 24.83 cm³ of 0.15 M NaOH is tritrated to its end point with 39.45 cm³ of HCl, what is the molarity of the HCl ?

Magnesium ribbon was allowed to burn inside a given gas P leaving a white solid residue Q. Addition of water to Q liberated a gas which produced dense white fumes with a drop of hydrochloric acid. The gas P was
exp: Mg burns in nitrogen to Mg₃N₂; with water this gives NH₃, which forms white NH₄Cl fumes with HCl.

q: The best treatment for a student who accidentally poured concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid on his skin in the laboratory is to wash he skin with
exp: Immediately flood the skin with plenty of cold water to dilute and remove the acid.

q: Which of the following gases can best be used for demonstrating the fountain experiment? (i) Nitrogen (ii) Ammonia (iii) Nitrogen (I)oxide (iv) Hydrogen chloride
exp: The fountain experiment needs extremely soluble gases — ammonia and hydrogen chloride.

q: When calcium hydroxide us heated with ammonium tetraoxosulphate (VI), the gas given off may be collected by
opts: Bubbling it through water and then passing it through calcium oxide
Passing it directly through calcium oxide
Passing it directly through calcium chloride.
exp: Ammonia is passed directly through calcium oxide, the only common drying agent that does not react with it.

q: Which of the following is used in fire extinguishers?
exp: CO₂ is dense and non-combustible — used in fire extinguishers.

q: Suitable regents for the laboratory preparation of nitrogen are
exp: Heating sodium trioxonitrate(III) (nitrite) with ammonium chloride gives nitrogen: NaNO₂ + NH₄Cl → NaCl + N₂ + 2H₂O.

q: The thermal decomposition of copper (II) trioxonirate (V) yields copper (II) oxide, oxygen and
exp: 2Cu(NO₃)₂ → 2CuO + 4NO₂ + O₂ — the brown gas is nitrogen(IV) oxide.

q: Which of the following is used in the manufacture of glass?
exp: Glass is made from sand, limestone and sodium trioxocarbonate(IV), Na₂CO₃.

q: The product of the thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonirate (V) are.
exp: NH₄NO₃ → N₂O + 2H₂O on gentle heating.

q: Equal volumes of CO, SO₂ NO₂ and H₂S, were released into a room at the same point and time. Which of the following gives the order of the room?
exp: Lighter gases diffuse faster: CO (28) > H₂S (34) > NO₂ (46) > SO₂ (64).

q: Which of the following samples will react faster with dilute dtrioxonitrate (V) acid?
opts: 5 g of lumps of CaCO₃ at 25oC
5 g of lumps of CaCO₃ at 50oC
exp: Powdering increases surface area and higher temperature increases collision energy — both speed the reaction.

q: Which of the following gases can be collected by upward displacement of air?
exp: Chlorine is denser than air, so it is collected by upward displacement of air.

q: Coal fire should not be used in poorly ventilated rooms because
opts: of the accumulation of CO₂ which cause deep sleep
of the accumulation of CO which causes suffocation
it removes most of the gases in the room
exp: In poor ventilation coal burns incompletely, producing carbon(II) oxide which is poisonous and causes suffocation.

q: A quantity of air was passed through a weighed mount of alkaline pyrogallol. An increase in the weight of the pyrogallol would result from the absorption of.
exp: Alkaline pyrogallol absorbs oxygen from the air.

q: 50 cm³ of sulphur (IV) oxide, 800cm³ of ammonia, 450 cm³ of hydrogen chloride, 1.0 cm³ of water at 15oC. Which of the following is suitable for demonstrating the fountain experiment?
exp: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride are extremely soluble — ideal for the fountain experiment.

q: Oxygen gas can be prepared by heating
exp: 2KNO₃ → 2KNO₂ + O₂ on heating.

q: Which of the following, in clear solution, forms a white precipitate when carbon(IV) oxide is bubbled into it for a short time?
exp: CO₂ turns lime water (Ca(OH)2) milky by forming insoluble CaCO₃.

q: Copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) is widely used as a
exp: Copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) is widely used as a fungicide (e.g. in Bordeaux mixture).

q: Which of the following oxides of nitrogen is unstable in air?
exp: NO reacts spontaneously with oxygen in air, forming brown NO₂ — it is unstable in air.

q: The gas formed when ammonium trioxonitrate (V) is heated with sodium hydroxide is
exp: An ammonium salt heated with an alkali always liberates ammonia.

q: Safety matches contain sulphur and
exp: Safety match heads contain sulphur with potassium trioxochlorate(V) as the oxidiser.

q: Which of the following is NOT used as raw material in the solvary process?
exp: Sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) is the PRODUCT of the Solvay process, not a raw material.

q: Water can be identified by the use of
exp: Anhydrous copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) turns from white to blue in the presence of water.

q: Which of these salts will produce its metal, oxygen and nitrogen(IV) oxide on heating?
exp: 2AgNO₃ → 2Ag + 2NO₂ + O₂ — silver nitrate decomposes right down to the metal.

q: Copper metal will react with concentrated trioxonitrate (V) acid to give
exp: Cu + 4HNO₃(conc) → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O.

q: Which of the following are produced when ammonium trioxonirate(V) crystals are cautiously heated in a hard glass round bottomed flask?
exp: Cautious heating of NH₄NO₃ gives dinitrogen oxide and steam.

q: Clothes should be properly rinsed with water after bleaching because
opts: chlorine reacts with fabrics during bleaching
the clothes are sterilized during bleaching
hydrogen chloride solution is produced during bleaching.
exp: Bleaching with chlorine leaves acidic products (HCl/HOCl) which would rot the fabric if not rinsed out.

q: Which of these solutions will give a white precipate with a solution of barium chloride acidified with hydrochloride acid?
exp: Only the sulphate gives a white BaSO₄ precipitate that persists in acid solution.

q: The number of hydrogen ions in 4.9 g of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acids is
exp: 4.9 g H₂SO₄ = 0.05 mol → 0.1 mol H⁺ = 6.02 × 10²² ions.

q: What volume of oxygen will remain after reacting 8 cm³ of hydrogen with 20 cm³ of oxygen?
exp: 8 cm³ H₂ consumes 4 cm³ O₂ (2:1), leaving 20 − 4 = 16 cm³ of oxygen.

q: A gas that will turn orange potassium heptaoxodichromate (VI) solution to clear green is
exp: SO₂ reduces orange dichromate to green Cr³⁺ — the standard SO₂ test.

q: In the extraction of iron in the blast furnace, limestone is used to
opts: Increase in the strenght of Iron
exp: Limestone decomposes to CaO which combines with silica impurities to form slag.

q: 35 cm³ of hydrogen was sparked with 12cm³ of oxygen at 110o C and 760 mm Hg to produce steam. What percentage of the total volume gas left after the reaction is hydrogen
exp: 12 cm³ O₂ burns 24 cm³ H₂, leaving 11 cm³ H₂ and 24 cm³ steam (gaseous at 110°C): 11/35 ≈ 31%.

q: 200cm³ of air was passed over heated copper in a syringe several times to produce copper (II) oxide. When cooled the final volume of air recorded was 158cm³. Estimate the percentage of oxygen in the air.
exp: Oxygen removed = 200 − 158 = 42 cm³; 42/200 = 21%.

q: A compound that will NOT produce oxygen on heating is
exp: Potassium dioxonitrate(III) (nitrite) does not give oxygen on heating; PbO₂ and KClO₃ both do.

q: The reaction that occurs during the laboratory test for the presence of tetraoxosulphate (VI)
exp: The sulphate test: Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → white BaSO₄, insoluble in dilute acid.

q: Which of the following additives could improve the quality of steel?
exp: Chromium and nickel make stainless steel — harder and corrosion resistant. Sulphur and phosphorus are harmful impurities.

q: 8.0 g of an element X reacted with an excess of copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (IV) solution to deposit 21.3 g of copper. The correct equation for the reaction is
exp: Cu deposited = 21.3/63.5 ≈ 0.335 mol; X = 8/24 ≈ 0.333 mol (magnesium) — a 1:1 ratio: X + CuSO₄ → Cu + XSO₄.

q: Excess phosphorus was burnt in gas jar and the residual gas passed successively over concentrated KOH solution and concentrated H₂SO₄ before being collected in a flask. The gases collected are
opts: carbon (IV) oxide nitrogen and the rare gases
nitrogen (IV) oxide and the rare gases
carbon (IV) oxide nitrogen (IV) oxide and the rare gases.
exp: Phosphorus removes O₂, KOH removes CO₂, H₂SO₄ dries the gas — leaving nitrogen and the rare gases.

q: In the conductance of aqueous potassium tetraoxosulphate (IV) solution, the current carriers are the
exp: In aqueous solution the current is carried by hydrated ions.

q: A gas that trun a filter paper previously soaked in lead ethanoate solution black is
exp: H₂S blackens lead ethanoate paper by forming black PbS.

q: A solution containing chloride gives a white precipitate with silver trioxonirate (V) solution. The precipitate will be insoluble in dilute
opts: HNO₃ but soluble in ammonia solution
HCI but soluble in ammonia solution
exp: AgCl is insoluble in dilute HNO₃ but dissolves in ammonia solution as [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺.

q: The gas that will form a white precipitate with acidified silver trioxonirate (V) is
exp: HCl gas gives a white precipitate of AgCl with acidified silver trioxonitrate(V).

q: 50cm³ of carbon (II) oxide was exploded with 150cm³ of air containing 20% oxygen by volume, which of the reactants was in excess?
exp: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂: 50 cm³ CO needs 25 cm³ O₂; the air supplies 30 cm³ — oxygen is in excess.

q: The chemical used for coagulation in water purification is
exp: Aluminium tetraoxosulphate(VI) (alum) coagulates suspended particles in water treatment.

q: Phosphorus is stored under water to prevent it from
exp: White phosphorus ignites spontaneously in air, so it is stored under water.

q: When chlorine is passed into water and the resulting solution exposed to sunlight, the products formed are
exp: Sunlight decomposes chlorine water into hydrochloric acid and oxygen.

q: The main impurity in iron ore during the extraction of iron is
exp: The main impurity in iron ore is silica (SiO₂), removed as slag with limestone.

q: A burning candle produces water and
exp: Burning hydrocarbons (candle wax) produces water and carbon(IV) oxide.

q: A compound contain 31.91% potassium, 28.93% chlorine and the rest oxygen. What is the chemical formula of the compound?
exp: Mole ratio K:Cl:O = 0.818:0.815:2.45 = 1:1:3 → KClO₃.

q: The gas that gives brown colouration in brown ring test is
exp: The brown ring is FeSO₄·NO — formed by nitrogen(II) oxide in the nitrate test.

q: An example of an element that can catenate is
exp: Carbon atoms bond to one another in long chains and rings — catenation.

q: When H₂S is passed into a solution of iron (iii) chloride, the solution turns
exp: Fe³⁺ (yellow-brown) is reduced by H₂S to pale green Fe²⁺.

q: Which of the following solutions containing only hydroxyl ions will liberate hydrogen gas when reacted with magnesium metal?
exp: [OH⁻] = 10⁻¹² means [H⁺] = 10⁻² — an acidic solution, the only one that reacts with Mg to give H₂.

q: Tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid burns the sk9in by
exp: Concentrated H₂SO₄ removes water from the skin tissue — dehydration.

q: Chlorine gas is prepared in the laboratory by
opts: adding concentrated hydrochloric acid to solid manganese (IV) oxide
adding concentrated tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid to solid sodium chloride
dropping concentrated hydrochloric acid onto potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII) crystals
oxidizing concentrated hydrochloric using potassium heptadichromate (VI) crystals.
exp: Laboratory chlorine: concentrated HCl on manganese(IV) oxide (heated).

q: Which of the following statements is true of sulphur (IV) oxide?
opts: It forms tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid with water
It forms white precipitate with acidified barium chloride.
exp: SO₂ is the anhydride of trioxosulphate(IV) acid: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃.

q: The salt that will form a precipitate soluble in excess ammonia solution is
exp: Cu(OH)2 dissolves in excess ammonia forming the deep-blue [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ complex.

q: If a solution contains 4.9g of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid, calculate the amount of copper (II) oxide that will react with it
exp: 4.9 g H₂SO₄ = 0.05 mol; CuO + H₂SO₄ is 1:1 → 0.05 × 80 = 4.0 g.

q: When steam is passed over red-hot carbon, the substances produced are
exp: C + H₂O → CO + H₂ (water gas).

q: Sulphur (IV) oxide bleaches by
exp: SO₂ bleaches by reduction — removing oxygen from the dye (the colour can return on oxidation).

q: Which of the following gases can be collected by the method of downward delivery?
exp: Chlorine is denser than air, so it is collected by downward delivery.

q: Stainless steel is an alloy of
exp: Stainless steel = iron + carbon + chromium (chromium gives the rust resistance).

q: Zn + H₂SO₄ ZnCI₂ + H₂ The rate of the above reaction will be greatly increased if.
opts: the zinc is in the powered form
a greater volume of the acid is used
a smaller volume of the acid is used
the reaction vessel is immersed in an ice-bath
the zinc is in the form of pellets.
exp: Powdering the zinc increases its surface area, greatly speeding the reaction.

q: A piece of sea shell, when dropped into a dilute solution of hydrochloric acid produces a colourless odorless gas, which turns clear limewater milky. The shell contains
exp: CO₂ evolved with acid turning lime water milky identifies calcium carbonate in the shell.

q: Mixing of aqueous solution of barium hydroxide and sodium tetraoxocarbonate(IV) yields a white precipitate of
exp: Ba(OH)2 + Na₂CO₃ → BaCO₃ (white precipitate) + 2NaOH.

q: Which of the following compounds is NOT the correct product formed when the parent metal is heated in air?
exp: Sodium burns in air to give mainly the peroxide Na₂O₂, not the simple oxide Na₂O.

q: Stainless steel is an alloy of
exp: Stainless steel is iron, carbon and chromium.

q: The formula of the compound formed in a reaction between a trivalent metal M and a tetravalent non-metal X is.
exp: M³⁺ with X⁴⁻: cross the valencies → M4X3.

q: Given the reactions (i) Fe(s) + (NO₃)₂(aq) Fe(NO₃)₂(aq) + X(s) (ii) H₂(g) + XO(s) X(s) + H₂O(g), X is likely to be.
exp: X is displaced by iron (below Fe) and its oxide is reduced by hydrogen — copper fits both.

q: Calcium hydroxide is added in the treatment of town water supply to
opts: improve the tase of the water.
exp: Calcium hydroxide helps coagulate suspended organic particles during water treatment.

q: A solution of calcium bromide contains 20 g dm³ What is the molarity of the solution with respect to calcium bromide and bromide ions?
exp: CaBr₂ (M = 200): 20 g/dm³ = 0.1 M; each unit gives 2Br⁻ → 0.2 M bromide.

q: In the reaction: SnO₂ + 2C Sn + 2CO the mass of coke containing 80% carbon required to reduce 0.032 kg of pure tin oxide is
exp: SnO₂ + 2C: carbon needed = 2 × 12 × (320/151) g ≈ 51 g; at 80% purity coke ≈ 0.06 kg (for 0.32 kg of oxide).

q: NaC₂O₄ + CaCl CaC₂O₄ + 2NaCl. Given a solution of 1.9 g of sodium oxalate in 50 g of water at room temperature, calculate the minimum volume of 0.1 M calcium oxalate required to produce maximum calcium oxalate using the above equation.
Which of the following metals will liberate hydrogen form steam or dilute acid?
exp: Of the options only iron is above hydrogen — it liberates H₂ from steam and dilute acids.

q: The major component of the slag from the production of iron is
opts: an alloy of calcium and iron
exp: Slag is mainly calcium trioxosilicate(IV), CaSiO₃.

q: Which of the following compounds gives a yellow residue when heated and also reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide to give a white gelatinous precipitate soluble in excess sodium hydroxide solution.
exp: ZnCO₃ → ZnO (yellow hot, white cold); Zn²⁺ gives a white gelatinous precipitate soluble in excess NaOH.
